teach.goal: Como não traduzir palavra por palavra.

facts.label: Experiências com ever e never
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio para experiências de vida: I have visited it twice. Pergunte Have you ever…? e responda Yes, I have ou No, I haven’t. Use never para nenhuma vez.

facts.label: Experiências
facts.sub: Para falar de experiências na vida, use have/has + particípio: I have visited the museum. Não diga quando aconteceu. Use ever em perguntas: Have you ever seen it? A resposta é Yes, I have ou No, I haven’t.

facts.label: Nunca
facts.sub: Never quer dizer em nenhum momento da vida. Use have never + particípio: I have never tasted the cake. Não use not com never. Na fala, I’ve never fica curto e fácil.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Have you ever been…? asks about life experiences.
items.why: Yes.

items.s: After have, we use the base verb.
items.why: We use the past participle.

items.s: “I have never seen it” is correct.
items.why: Yes.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.

answers: Have you ever been…? asks about life experiences. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
After have, we use the base verb. → Falso (We use the past participle.)
“I have never seen it” is correct. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 2/2

items.s: We say “Have you ever went there?”
items.why: We say Have you ever gone there? or been there.

items.s: Never already has a negative meaning.
items.why: So we do not say “I have never not seen it”.

answers: We say “Have you ever went there?” → Falso (We say Have you ever gone there? or been there.)

pages.title: A day at the museum · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy Saturday morning in Boston. A long line of people waits outside the old museum. Ana holds two tickets and a small map. Her friend Sam arrives with a wet umbrella. Neither of them knows every room in the building. They start by talking about what they have done here.

“Hi, Ana! Have you ever been to this museum before?” says Sam. “Yes, I have. I have visited it twice with my school.” says Ana. “Really? I have never seen the big painting on the second floor.” says Sam.
